q1_issues.issue: `Forbid` is licensed only as the seal for a NEGATIVE IMPERATIVE ("Don't open the hatch"), so using it to carry the negation of a declarative that-clause makes the parse read as a command to forbid entry rather than a command to ensure nobody enters.
The negative-quantifier subject "nobody" is dropped entirely: the go event has no Agent, no person witness or kind atom is minted, and no strength-0.0 / QuantifierPhrase carrier records the "no".
`there` stands as a bare untyped constant in the Location slot, against the rule that an untyped referent symbol must never appear in the output.
"goes in there" is a motion verb with a directional PP, so the where-adjunct `Location` is the wrong oblique for what the clause states.

q2_gaps: "make sure / ensure that P" — a finite that-clause complement of a verb that is neither an attitude, an embedded question, an imperative nor a counterfactual; no sealing route covers it

a negative-quantifier subject ("nobody" / "no one") inside a sealed complement — a seal has no polarity carrier, so the strength-0.0 encoding of "no" cannot be expressed there (registered for reported attitudes, but no encoding is licensed for this case)
deictic locative pro-forms ("there", "here") — deictic TIMES are given speech-anchored bare constants, but no rule covers a deictic place
notes: Every head used is a defined operator, but `Forbid` is applied outside the one construction that licenses it. The outer `Directive` wrapper and the tenseless, addressee-free make_sure reification are correct.
